1) cocultivation of two clonal stromal lines, which display different gamma-irradiated responses relative to dose rates, results in changes in radiation-induced cell killing, 2) these changes are consistent with preferencial killing of the more sensitive stromal cell line, and 3) the radiation survival curve of the cocultivated cell lines was always characteristic of the resistant line, even when it was present in large numbers.

the effect of cocultivation on the gamma-irradiator response of bone marrow stromal cells.

a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying the heterogeneity of the gamma- irradiation response of the bone marrow micro-environment, with the ultimate aim to identify stromal cells that could potentially protect the hematopoietic compartment against radiation-induced damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intrinsic radiosensitivity is not altered during cocultivation of two stromal cell lines with distinct radiosensitivity, but the repair of radiation induced damage is modified, and the more resistant cell line has a dominant effect.
cocultivation with the gamma-irr resistant KM 104 cell line induces an increase in the gamma- irradiation resistance of the more sensitive KM 101 cell line, and vice-versa.
the gamma-irradiator response of a cocultivated stromalistromal cell line system, is determined by the gamma-irradition response of the more radiosensistive cell line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intrinsic radiosensitivity is a function of both cell line and the dose rate of irradiation.
the intrinsic radiosensitivity is not a fixed property of the cells, but is influenced by the cellular environment.
cocultivation, before, during, or after gamma irradiation, can alter the intrinsic radiosensitivity, and that a resistant cell line has a dominant effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gamma-irradiator response of cocultured stromal cell lines is dependent upon the intrinsic radiosensitivity, and the relative number of cells in each cell line.

the gamma-iradiation response of a stromal cell line may depend not only on intrinsic radiosensitivity of the cell line, but also on the microenvironment in which the cell is located, as well as the dose rate of irradiation.
cocultivation can alter the intrinsic radiosensitivity, and the repair of radiation-induced DNA damage of stromal cells.
